items.evidence: Vanilla 26.2 PistonBaseBlock.isPushable (net.minecraft.world.level.block.piston.PistonBaseBlock, jar-verified) bounds-checks y > maxY (320; overworld dimension_type min_y -64 + height 384) and refuses only UP-pushes from y == maxY. The port uses max_y = level.max_y() - 1 (319) at level/pistons.rs:337, so it refuses y == 320 outright and refuses UP-pushes from y == 319. A piston at y == 319 pushing up fails in the port where vanilla extends. Floor side matches vanilla exactly. 1.21.7 G10 survives in 26.2.
items.title: is_pushable Y-bound off by one at the ceiling

items.evidence: tools/test_piston_shape_parity.py:63 asserts len(facts['states']) == 35723, so it fails outright on 26.2 before comparing anything. 26.2 has 32,366 states (docs/sweep/26.2/inventory.md, from the 26.2 datagen reports). The oracle (VanillaPistonShapeOracle) compiles clean against the 26.2 jars (Batch 0 measurement, all three classpaths); the driver constant is the defect. No other Batch 2 driver hardcodes 35723. 1.21.7 G13 survives in 26.2.

items.evidence: Batch 0 measurement (docs/sweep/26.2/batch-0-oracles.json): fails on all three classpaths, 1 error, '188: cannot find symbol'. The symbol is datapackWorldRegistries() on the WorldLoader load-context (VanillaRedstoneCatalogOracle.java:188). 26.2's WorldLoader$DataLoadContext (jar-verified) has no such accessor — its record components are resources(), dataConfiguration(), datapackWorldgen(), datapackDimensions(); datapackWorldRegistries() is the 26.3 name. The 26.2 equivalent for the world-preset lookup is datapackDimensions(). Blocks test_redstone_catalog_parity only.

systemic_note: The 26.2 tree is the 1.21.11-template lineage, and it shows: all three 1.21.7 majors (G7 wire class name, G8 push-reaction loader, G9 obsidian hardcode) are fixed at the template and carried into 26.2, and five of six Batch 2 oracles compile clean for 26.2 (vs one of six for 1.21.7). The remaining gaps are the template's leftovers, not new 26.2 regressions: the Y-bound off-by-one (B2-G01) and the two driver constants (B2-G02/B2-G03). Two 1.21.7 defects (G11, G12) do not apply to 26.2 at all — vanilla itself changed between 1.21.7 and 26.2 (comparator takes max(frame, block); moveBlocks destroys with setBlock(air, 18)), and the port matches 26.2's form. The vanilla-check rule mattered in both directions here: assuming the 1.21.7 form would have filed two false defects, and assuming the 26.3 form (PushReaction renames, obsidian IMMOVEABLE, datapackWorldRegistries) would have missed the real ones.

withdrawn.evidence: 1.21.7's G11 was that vanilla takes the item frame first and the port takes max(frame, block). In 26.2 vanilla CHANGED: ComparatorBlock.getInputSignal (bytecode offsets 98-164) computes Math.max(frameAnalogOrMIN, blockAnalogOrMIN) and uses it unless both are absent — vanilla 26.2 takes the max, exactly as the port does (level/redstone.rs:543-549). The port matches 26.2; no defect. (1.21.7 G11 stands for 1.21.7 only.)
